record.original_question: For Leroy Quet's sequence defined by a_1=1, a_2=2, and for n≥3 choosing a_n as the smallest unused positive integer such that gcd(a_n,a_{n-1}) differs from gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2}), explain why the associated 4-regular graph has the observed nontrivial structure and decide whether that structural behavior continues for arbitrarily large initial segments.

evidence.quote: It is given by a_1 = 1, a_2 = 2 and then by picking a_n as the smallest positive integer that has not yet occurred in the sequence satisfying the property that gcd(a_n, a_{n-1}) ≠ gcd(a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}).
We obtain a graph that clearly exhibits some nontrivial structure – it is not clear to us why or whether it will continue in this fashion (see Fig. 11).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define a sequence $(a_n)_{n\geq 1}$ of positive integers as follows. Set $a_1=1$ and $a_2=2$. For each $n\geq 3$, let $a_n$ be the smallest positive integer that has not yet appeared among $a_1,\dots,a_{n-1}$ and that satisfies
$$\gcd(a_n,a_{n-1}) \neq \gcd(a_{n-1},a_{n-2}).$$
For each integer $N\geq 1$, build a 4-regular graph $G_N$ on the vertex set $\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_N\}$ by joining each term to its two immediate predecessors and two immediate successors in the sequence (so vertex $a_n$ is adjacent to $a_{n-2}, a_{n-1}, a_{n+1}, a_{n+2}$ when these exist). 

Numerical computation of $G_N$ for moderately large $N$ reveals a striking nontrivial visual/combinatorial structure (clusters, bands, or regular patterns rather than apparent randomness).

(a) Give a rigorous explanation of the observed nontrivial structure of $G_N$ in terms of the arithmetic of the sequence $(a_n)$.

(b) Determine whether this structural behavior persists for arbitrarily large $N$, or whether it eventually breaks down.
artifact.status_search_result: The underlying sequence is OEIS A127202, contributed by Leroy Quet (2007). The OEIS entry and related discussion record empirical observations and conjectures (e.g., that it is a permutation of the positive integers) but do not contain a structural explanation of the associated 4-regular adjacency graph nor a proof that the observed visual structure persists. No published resolution of the structural question was located.
